_comment:
House drafting standard. One file, reused for every job -- the job itself is an intake workbook, not a config.

The difference from sld_config*.json: those name an absolute sheet elevation for every device, so a cubicle that lacks a device needs a whole new archetype at new elevations. That is why 'two CTs' ended up baked into type NAMES, and why two-high decks are blocked. Here a device declares only its gap from the device above it, and the builder stacks whatever the intake row actually calls for.

A device is drawn if and only if its 'when' column has a value in the unit row. No archetype inherits a device from a drawing it was copied from.

sheet._pitch_note: All units drawn to the widest, per IOM practice. Overridden by --pitch.
sheet._frame_note: Symmetric about the bus: 9.148 of cubicle each side, so a two-high cubicle gives both decks the same room and the bus lands at the mid level. The lower deck takes its cable out through the floor, the upper deck out through the roof, exactly as each other's mirror image.
sheet._bus_label_note: Filled from the Project tab rather than fixed in the config, so the bus label can never disagree with the job it was drawn for.

_stack_note: Ordered top to bottom. 'gap' is the drop from the previous PRESENT device's anchor to this one's, so a skipped device closes the stack up rather than leaving a hole. Gaps measured off sld_config_assignment.json, which reproduces them exactly when every device is present.

stack.name: drawout_upper
stack._gap_note: From bus_y down to the upper primary disconnect.
stack._when_note: The primary disconnects are the breaker's own drawout contacts, so they come and go with it. A deck holding only a bus PT has no breaker to rack out.

stack.name: breaker
stack._when_note: A cubicle without a breaker rating has no breaker. That is what lets a deck hold only a bus PT.

stack.name: drawout_lower
stack._when_note: The primary disconnects are the breaker's own drawout contacts, so they come and go with it. A deck holding only a bus PT has no breaker to rack out.

stack.name: ct_metering
stack._note: The device that used to arrive uninvited. It appears only when the intake row states a metering ratio.

_branch_note: The bus PT hangs on a shunt tap ABOVE the bus, so neither it nor its primary fuse ever lands in the main conductor path between the bus and the breaker. Stacks upward from bus_y; risers are generated between consecutive devices.

pinned.name: outgoing
pinned._y_note: The cable exit sits at the cubicle floor, so it is pinned rather than stacked -- a unit with fewer CTs must not raise its own cable termination. But a unit carrying all three CTs stacks past 9.034, so the pin gives way and the exit is pushed down to clear the last device by push_gap. Without that a third CT lands below its own cable termination.

relay_box._note: Outline around the relay label, which annotate_unit prints from the 'relay' column.

ct_compartment._note: Sized from the CTs actually present instead of from a remembered span. On a unit with a protection and a ground CT this yields 12.378..9.907, against the 12.465..9.912 drawn by hand on 8508 -- so the rule reproduces the reference without copying its number.

phase_note._note: Single-phase mark beside a CT. %%C is AutoCAD's phase symbol.

conductor._note: The vertical run down the cubicle centreline. build_sld draws it between the series roles' gaps.

_decks_note: A two-high cubicle holds two breakers on one centreline, one row per deck, both rows carrying the same unit number. The upper deck is the lower deck reflected about the bus: same devices, same gaps, same symbols, running upward and taking its cable out through the roof. Reflecting rather than re-measuring is what makes the second deck free -- there is no second set of elevations to keep in step with the first.

upper._text_shift_note: MTEXT hangs downward from its insertion point, so reflecting the anchor alone would leave a four-line spec block growing out of the bottom of the breaker it belongs to. Each style is nudged up by roughly its own rendered height. These are the redline knobs -- adjust here if a label sits proud.
upper._hide_text_note: The unit number and tag describe the cubicle, and both decks share one. Printing them from each row stacks two headers at the same elevation. The upper deck's own tag and ratings still appear in its spec block beside its breaker.

_control_note: Lineup-wide horizontal runs. The bus PT's voltage reference is one of these, not a per-unit device: it originates at whichever unit states a 'pt' and drops into every unit that states a 'relay'. So it re-routes itself when the PT moves to a different cubicle, and it reaches exactly the units that have something to reference it.

buses.name: pt_reference
buses._end_dx_note: Must reach the LAST riser, not the last centreline. The risers drop at +1.336 (the relay box centre), so an end_dx of 0 leaves the final unit's drop hanging in mid-air just short of the run. start_dx stays 0 because the run originates under the PT cubicle's own centreline.
buses._y_note: Below the relay boxes (bottom 14.043) and above the CT compartment (top 12.378), so it crosses neither. The riser at dx 1.336 is the relay box centreline, clear of the compartment's -1.081..0.290 span.
buses._note: A run needs two participants to be drawn, so a single-unit lineup, or one where only the PT cubicle carries a relay, correctly produces no run at all.
